answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, each identity locks its own refundable smart-contract bond, making multiple identities costly. Only when cryptographic proof shows conflicting commitments signed for the same task, the slash is executed. Like a sable night, the system remains vigilant, waiting for discrepancies to surface. The umber of false identities is reduced, making it harder for attackers to succeed. On the island of trust, this mechanism ensures a secure and decentralized network.
